items.front: Where and when did the Bhakti movement first flower, and through whom?
items.back: South India (7th-12th c.) through the Nayanars (Shaiva) and Alvars (Vaishnava).
items.examPoint: Bhakti roots & causes (South India 7th–12th c.; response to orthodoxy, Jainism & Buddhism)

items.front: Saguna vs Nirguna Bhakti — the difference and key saints?
items.back: Saguna = God with form (Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai); Nirguna = formless (Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas).

items.front: Alvars vs Nayanars — deity, number and canon?
items.back: Alvars = 12 Vaishnava (Nalayira Divya Prabandham); Nayanars = 63 Shaiva (Tevaram).
items.examPoint: Alvars — Vaishnava, 12 saints, Nalayira Divya Prabandham, Andal

items.front: Match the three acharyas to their Vedanta schools.
items.back: Shankara = Advaita; Ramanuja = Vishishtadvaita; Madhva = Dvaita.

items.front: Shankaracharya's doctrine and his four mathas?
items.back: Advaita (Atman=Brahman, world is Maya); mathas at Badrinath, Puri, Dwarka, Sringeri.
items.examPoint: Adi Shankaracharya — Advaita Vedanta & four mathas

items.front: Who founded Lingayatism, and its key features?
items.back: Basavanna (12th-c. Karnataka); Ishtalinga worship, Vachana poetry, Anubhava Mantapa; rejected caste.
items.examPoint: Virashaivism & Lingayatism — Basavanna, Ishtalinga, Vachana, Akka Mahadevi

items.front: Whose disciple was Kabir, and where are his verses found?
items.back: Ramananda's disciple; Nirguna verses in the Bijak, Kabir Granthavali and the Adi Granth.
items.examPoint: Kabir — Nirguna, Bijak/dohas, critique of ritual & caste

items.front: Guru Nanak's three pillars of teaching?
items.back: Naam Japna, Kirat Karna, Vand Chhakna; also introduced Langar and Sangat.
items.examPoint: Guru Nanak & Sikhism — Nirguna, Langar, Nam Japna/Kirat Karna/Vand Chhakna

items.front: Maharashtra Varkari saints and their focus deity?
items.back: Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram — devoted to Vithoba of Pandharpur; sang Abhangas.
items.examPoint: Maharashtra Varkari saints — Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram; Pandharpur/Vithoba

items.front: Chishti silsilah — founder in India and famous figures?
items.back: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (Ajmer); embraced sama, avoided politics; Nizamuddin Auliya, Amir Khusrau.
items.examPoint: Chishti silsilah — Muinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Nizamuddin Auliya, Amir Khusrau

items.front: Match Sufi silsilahs to figures: Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi, Qadiri.
items.back: Suhrawardi = Bahauddin Zakariya (Multan); Naqshbandi = Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi; Qadiri = Miyan Mir.
items.examPoint: Other Sufi silsilahs — Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi (Sirhindi), Qadiri (Miyan Mir/Dara Shikoh)

items.front: Telugu Bhakti: who sang to Venkateswara, and who to Rama of Bhadrachalam?
items.back: Annamacharya (Tirupati sankirtanas); Bhadrachala Ramadasu (Bhadrachalam); Tyagaraja = Carnatic Trinity.
items.examPoint: Telugu Bhakti — Bhadrachala Ramadasu & Tyagaraja (Carnatic Trinity)
